step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identify core visual nodes from the visual inventory and transcript: Amplify (RCC Hours app), Step Functions (Diablo batch orchestration), Aurora MySQL (centerpiece store), Lambda Exporter (menu generator), Delivery Aggregator (third-party endpoint), API Gateway (webhook endpoint), and Lambda Webhook (audit processor).
2. Normalize services against the allowed AWS list: Amplify -> Amplify, StepFunctions -> StepFunctions, Aurora -> Aurora, Lambda Exporter -> Lambda, Delivery Aggregator -> ThirdParty, API Gateway -> ApiGateway, Lambda Webhook -> Lambda.
3. Assign sequential string IDs ('0' through '6') to nodes.
4. Trace distinct logical flows:
   - Flow 0: Store hours entry via Amplify writing to Aurora.
   - Flow 1: Batch product, pricing, and tax updates orchestrated by Diablo Step Functions writing to Aurora.
   - Flow 2: Menu exporter Lambda reading data from Aurora and pushing generated JSON menus to Delivery Aggregators.
   - Flow 3: Delivery Aggregators returning status webhooks through API Gateway to the Webhook Lambda, which writes audit records into Aurora.

graph.name: Taco Bell Menu Middleware and Data Integration Platform
graph.notes: Architecture for Taco Bell's menu middleware, serving over 7,000 restaurants and generating roughly 40,000 menus (100GB of JSON menu payload) sent to delivery aggregators.

nodes.name: Amplify
nodes.notes: Deploys the Restaurant Control Center (RCC) React web application used to update store hours.

nodes.name: Step Functions
nodes.notes: Powers 'Diablo' (Data Integration and Automation Batch Lambda Orchestration) using reusable Python step types to load product master, pricing, and tax data.

nodes.name: Aurora
nodes.notes: Aurora MySQL database serving as the central middleware store containing restaurant hours, product data, and 100+ million pricing/tax combinations.

nodes.name: Lambda (Exporter)
nodes.notes: Generates 40,000 custom JSON menus totaling 100GB of data for delivery aggregator platforms.

nodes.name: DELIVERY AGGREGATOR
nodes.notes: External delivery partner platforms receiving generated menus and returning completion status webhooks.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: Receives completion webhooks from external delivery aggregator platforms.

nodes.name: Lambda (Webhook)
nodes.notes: Processes completion webhooks to log execution status into Aurora audit tables.

edges.notes: Amplify app writes updated store hours into Aurora database tables.
Step Functions orchestrates batch loading of product, pricing, and tax data into Aurora.
Menu Exporter Lambda reads restaurant hours, products, and pricing data from Aurora.
Exporter Lambda pushes generated JSON menu files to Delivery Aggregators.
Delivery Aggregators send processing status webhooks to API Gateway.
API Gateway triggers the Webhook Lambda to process incoming delivery notifications.
Webhook Lambda records processing status and audit logs in Aurora.
